sentences: Among the annoying challenges facing the middle class is one that will probably go unmentioned in the next presidential campaign: What happens when the robots come for their jobs?
translations: 中产阶级面临的恼人挑战中，有一个很可能在下一届总统竞选中不会被提及：当机器人来抢他们的工作时会发生什么？

sentences: Don’t dismiss that possibility entirely.
About half of U.S. jobs are at high risk of being automated, according to a University of Oxford study, with the middle class disproportionately squeezed.
Lower-income jobs like gardening or day care don’t appeal to robots.
But many middle-class occupations—trucking, financial advice, software engineering—have aroused their interest, or soon will.
The rich own the robots, so they will be fine.
translations: 不要完全否定这种可能性。
根据牛津大学的一项研究，美国约有一半的工作面临被自动化的高风险，中产阶级受到的挤压尤为严重。
像园艺或日托这样的低收入工作对机器人没有吸引力。
但许多中产阶级职业——卡车运输、金融咨询、软件工程——已经引起了它们的兴趣，或者很快就会引起。
富人拥有机器人，所以他们会没事的。

sentences: This isn’t to be alarmist.
Optimists point out that technological upheaval has benefited workers in the past.
The Industrial Revolution didn’t go so well for Luddites whose jobs were displaced by mechanized looms, but it eventually raised living standards and created more jobs than it destroyed.
Likewise, automation should eventually boost productivity, stimulate demand by driving down prices, and free workers from hard, boring work.
But in the medium term, middle-class workers may need a lot of help adjusting.
translations: 这并不是要危言耸听。
乐观主义者指出，过去的技术变革曾使工人受益。
工业革命对工作被机械化织布机取代的卢德分子来说并不顺利，但它最终提高了生活水平，创造的就业机会多于摧毁的。
同样，自动化最终应该会提高生产率，通过压低价格刺激需求，并将工人从艰苦、乏味的工作中解放出来。
但在中期，中产阶级工人可能需要大量帮助来适应。

sentences: The first step, as Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee argue in The Second Machine Age, should be rethinking education and job training.
Curriculums—from grammar school to college—should evolve to focus less on memorizing facts and more on creativity and complex communication.
Vocational schools should do a better job of fostering problem-solving skills and helping students work alongside robots.
Online education can supplement the traditional kind.
It could make extra training and instruction affordable.
Professionals trying to acquire new skills will be able to do so without going into debt.
translations: 正如埃里克·布林约尔松和安德鲁·麦卡菲在《第二次机器时代》中所论证的，第一步应该是重新思考教育和职业培训。
从文法学校到大学的课程设置应该演变，减少对死记硬背事实的关注，更多地关注创造力和复杂的沟通。
职业学校应该更好地培养解决问题的能力，并帮助学生与机器人并肩工作。
在线教育可以补充传统教育。
它可以使额外的培训和指导变得负担得起。
试图获得新技能的专业人士将能够做到这一点，而不会负债。

sentences: The challenge of coping with automation underlines the need for the U.S. to revive its fading business dynamism: Starting new companies must be made easier.
In previous eras of drastic technological change, entrepreneurs smoothed the transition by dreaming up ways to combine labor and machines.
The best uses of 3D printers and virtual reality haven’t been invented yet.
The U.S. needs the new companies that will invent them.
translations: 应对自动化的挑战凸显了美国重振其日渐衰退的商业活力的必要性：必须让创办新公司变得更容易。
在以往技术剧烈变革的时代，企业家通过构想将劳动力与机器相结合的方式，使转型得以平稳进行。
3D打印机和虚拟现实的最佳用途尚未被发明出来。
美国需要那些将发明这些用途的新公司。

sentences: Finally, because automation threatens to widen the gap between capital income and labor income, taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought.

Taxes on low-wage labor need to be cut, and wage subsidies such as the earned income tax credit should be expanded: This would boost incomes, encourage work, reward companies for job creation, and reduce inequality.
translations: 最后，由于自动化有可能扩大资本收入和劳动收入之间的差距，税收和社会保障体系将不得不重新考虑。
需要削减对低工资劳动力的税收，并扩大诸如劳动所得税抵免之类的工资补贴：这将提高收入，鼓励工作，奖励创造就业的公司，并减少不平等。

sentences: Technology will improve society in ways big and small over the next few years, yet this will be little comfort to those who find their lives and careers upended by automation.
Destroying the machines that are coming for our jobs would be nuts.
But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable.
translations: 在未来几年，技术将在或大或小的方面改善社会，然而对于那些发现自己的生活和事业被自动化颠覆的人来说，这几乎算不上什么安慰。
摧毁那些来抢我们工作的机器将是疯狂的。
但帮助工人适应的政策将是不可或缺的。

sentences:
21. Who will be most threatened by automation?
A. Leading politicians.
B. Low-wage laborers.
C. Robot owners.
D. Middle-class workers.
translations:
21. 谁将最受自动化的威胁？
A. 主要政治家。
B. 低薪劳动者。
C. 机器人所有者。
D. 中产阶级工人。

sentences:
22. Which of the following best represents the author’s view?
A. Worries about automation are in fact groundless.
B. Optimists’ opinions on new tech find little support.
C. Issues arising from automation need to be tackled.
D. Negative consequences of new tech can be avoided.
translations:
22. 以下哪项最能代表作者的观点？
A. 对自动化的担忧实际上是没有根据的。
B. 乐观主义者关于新技术的观点几乎得不到支持。
C. 自动化引发的问题需要得到解决。
D. 新技术带来的负面后果是可以避免的。

sentences:
23. Education in the age of automation should put more emphasis on
A. creative potential.
B. job-hunting skills.
C. individual needs.
D. cooperative spirit.
translations:
23. 在自动化时代，教育应更加注重
A. 创造潜力。
B. 求职技能。
C. 个人需求。
D. 合作精神。

sentences:
24. The author suggests that tax policies be aimed at
A. encouraging the development of automation.
B. increasing the return on capital investment.
C. easing the hostility between rich and poor.
D. preventing the income gap from widening.
translations:
24. 作者建议税收政策应旨在
A. 鼓励自动化的发展。
B. 提高资本投资的回报率。
C. 缓解富人与穷人之间的敌意。
D. 防止收入差距扩大。

sentences:
25. In this text, the author presents a problem with
A. opposing views on it.
B. possible solutions to it.
C. its alarming impacts.
D. its major variations.
translations:
25. 在这篇文章中，作者提出了一个问题，并
A. 对其持相反观点。
B. 给出了可能的解决方案。
C. 指出了其令人担忧的影响。
D. 说明了其主要变化形式。
